name: verify_signature
summary: Check whether an app or binary is code-signed and, if so, by whom — reports the signing authority chain, the developer's Team ID, and whether the signature is intact. Use for 'is this app properly signed / who signed it / has it been tampered with'. Read-only; runs codesign in verify mode only (it can never sign or modify anything).

params.name: path
params.description: App bundle (.app) or executable to verify, e.g. /Applications/Safari.app. Leading ~ ok; must not start with '-' (use ./).

name: gatekeeper_check
summary: Ask macOS Gatekeeper whether it would ALLOW an app to run — the same trust check that happens when you first open a downloaded app. Reports accepted/rejected plus the source (Developer ID, notarized, App Store, etc.). Use for 'is this app safe to open / will Gatekeeper block it'. Read-only assessment; spctl runs in --assess mode only and never enables/disables Gatekeeper.

params.name: path
params.description: App bundle (.app) or executable to assess, e.g. /Applications/Some.app. Leading ~ ok; must not start with '-' (use ./).

name: sip_status
summary: Report whether System Integrity Protection (SIP) — the macOS kernel-level protection that stops even admin/root from modifying system files — is enabled or disabled. Use for 'is SIP on / is my Mac's system protection enabled'. Read-only; csrutil is invoked only with 'status' and can never change SIP (which in any case requires Recovery mode).

name: quarantine_info
summary: Report whether a file carries the macOS 'quarantine' flag — the com.apple.quarantine attribute macOS attaches to files downloaded from the internet, which triggers the 'are you sure you want to open this?' prompt. Shows which app downloaded it and when, or 'not quarantined'. Use for 'was this file downloaded / why does macOS warn about opening it'. Read-only; xattr only reads the attribute (never writes or clears it).

params.name: path
params.description: File to inspect for the quarantine flag, e.g. ~/Downloads/installer.dmg. Leading ~ ok; must not start with '-' (use ./).

name: find_credential
summary: Check whether a saved password exists in the login keychain for an app or service, and report only its non-secret metadata — the service name, account/username, label, and when it was created/modified. Use for 'do I have a saved password for X / what account did I store for Y'. Read-only and secret-safe: it runs `security find-generic-password` WITHOUT the -w/-g flags, so the password value itself is never requested or shown. Give at least one of service or account to narrow the search.

params.name: service
params.description: The service/app name the password is stored under, e.g. 'AirPort' or 'com.example.app'. Must not start with '-'. Provide this, account, or both.

params.name: account
params.description: The account/username the password is stored for, e.g. 'jane@example.com'. Must not start with '-'. Provide this, service, or both.

name: find_internet_credential
summary: Check whether a saved internet password exists (a website/server login) and report only its non-secret metadata — the server, account, protocol, path, and dates. Use for 'do I have a saved login for example.com'. Read-only and secret-safe: it runs `security find-internet-password` WITHOUT the -w/-g flags, so the password value is never requested or shown. Give at least one of server or account.

params.name: server
params.description: The server/host the login is stored under, e.g. 'example.com'. Must not start with '-'. Provide this, account, or both.

params.name: account
params.description: The account/username the login is stored for, e.g. 'jane'. Must not start with '-'. Provide this, server, or both.

name: list_keychains
summary: List the keychain files on the search list (typically the user's login keychain and the system keychain). Use for 'what keychains do I have / where are my passwords stored'. Read-only; runs `security list-keychains` with a fixed argument list and shows only file paths, never any stored secret.
